area: Phaser 3.90 performance (render flags, pooling, atlases/generated textures, Arcade physics) — adjudicated for a 2-fighter procedural-vector duel scene

items.title: roundPixels silently defaults TRUE since Phaser 3.70 — set it explicitly to false to match the Flash sub-pixel vector look
items.claim: Phaser 3.70+ flipped the GameConfig default to roundPixels: true (pixel-snap via a uRoundPixels shader uniform in the texture pipelines); the repo's GameConfig in src/main.ts sets no render block, so on phaser@3.90 the game is running with rounding ON without anyone having chosen it. It affects texture-based objects (all the Text nameplates/HUD labels, several positioned at fractional x like 799 + i*73.5 and repositioned per frame to track fighters), NOT Graphics paths. Community reports (GitHub #6509, discourse) document jitter from the rounding when objects track smooth positions. The OG is a Flash vector game rendered sub-pixel; snapping is a divergence from source behavior, not an optimization.

items.adjudication_reason: src/main.ts GameConfig sets only type/width/height/backgroundColor/transparent/scale — no render block, so the 3.70+ roundPixels:true default is active by accident; DuelScene.drawFighters repositions texts.nameplate/playerName every frame from worldToStage output, exactly the tracking pattern the jitter reports describe, and the OG source is sub-pixel Flash vector.
items.implementation_note: Add render: { roundPixels: false } (and leave antialias at its default true — correct for the Flash vector look) to the Phaser.Game config in src/main.ts, then re-run the in-browser fidelity gate (?fidelity=auto / __fidelity.run()) since text glyph placement can shift by <1px and the gate samples real canvas pixels.

items.title: Bake the static arena Graphics into a runtime-generated texture (generateTexture) — the one atlas-adjacent idea that fits the invariant
items.claim: Official Phaser docs: Graphics are decomposed into polygons every render under WebGL — 'expensive processes, especially with complex shapes' — and the blessed fix for Graphics that never change is generateTexture(), which bakes the command list into a GPU texture drawn as one quad. DuelScene.drawArena() emits ~60+ fills/ellipses/rects (bamboo rows, canopy, mounds, lanterns) into a persistent Graphics that Phaser re-tessellates every frame despite never changing. generateTexture is a canvas/GPU runtime texture — no image FILE is created, so the no-asset-files invariant is untouched.

items.adjudication_reason: DuelScene.drawArena() is drawn once in create() into a Graphics that is re-tessellated per frame; src/game/CLAUDE.md bans image asset FILES, not runtime textures, so a generateTexture bake is invariant-compatible — but the 55/55 fidelity gate (src/game/fidelity.ts) samples real canvas pixels, and a texture round-trip can shift antialiased edges, so the bake must be gate-verified.
items.implementation_note: In drawArena(): draw to the Graphics, g.generateTexture('arena', GAME_WIDTH, GAME_HEIGHT), g.destroy(), this.add.image(0,0,'arena').setOrigin(0). Only do this if a profile (renderer.snapshot timing or DevTools GPU trace) shows draw cost at all — at 2 fighters the scene almost certainly holds 60fps already, so treat as insurance for the crowd EncounterScene, then re-run __fidelity.run() for 55/55.
items.stage: later — only on a measured frame-time problem (EncounterScene crowd growth is the likely trigger)

items.title: Texture-atlas advice: inapplicable — DuelScene has zero Sprites, and file atlases are banned anyway
items.claim: Atlas advice (pack sprites into one sheet to cut texture swaps and draw calls; practitioner post cites ~300KB download savings and fewer batch flushes) presumes texture-based Sprites. This scene renders fighters as Earcut-triangulated polygon fills (drawPlan in OgArtScene.ts) plus Graphics strokes — there are no textures to atlas, so batch-flush-from-texture-swap, the problem atlases solve, cannot occur here. File-based atlases would additionally violate the procedural-art invariant; the permitted runtime-texture variant is already covered by the arena-bake item.

items.title: Object pooling: the expensive pattern it prevents is already absent — FX records are plain JS objects, not GameObjects
items.claim: Pooling advice (Groups with maxSize, setActive(false) recycling; practitioner measured ~15% fps from pooling bullets/enemies) targets games creating/destroying hundreds of GameObjects per second, where each destroy tears down WebGL/display-list state and churns GC. This repo never creates GameObjects at runtime: droplets/trails/redStrokes are plain {x,y,vx,vy,bornAt} literals in arrays, all Text objects are created once in createHudTexts(), and EncounterScene deliberately draws damage-popup digits as Graphics blocks instead of Text objects. At BLOOD_COUNT-scale allocation (~a dozen small literals per hit) modern-GC pressure is negligible; adding a pool would be pure churn.

items.title: powerPreference / batchSize tuning: no-op at this scene's load — leave defaults
items.claim: Defaults on 3.90: powerPreference 'default', batchSize 4096 (vertex quads per flush). batchSize matters only when a single batch exceeds 4096 quads — this scene submits two tessellated fighters, ~40 droplet circles, and HUD rects, orders of magnitude below the limit, and Graphics style changes flush batches anyway so a bigger buffer buys nothing. powerPreference: 'high-performance' forces the discrete GPU on dual-GPU laptops — a battery cost with zero benefit for a scene this light; the practitioner postmortem even found WebGL→Canvas FASTER on a weak device, underlining that GPU-side tuning is not where this class of game is bound.

items.title: Arcade physics settings: nothing to tune — the repo intentionally has no physics engine
items.claim: Standard Arcade advice (fixedStep/fps tuning, useTree spatial index off for few bodies, Group-based overlap culling, only-check-active-bodies) configures Phaser's physics world. This repo runs zero Phaser physics: collision, movement, and projectiles are owned by the pure fixed-60Hz Sim with injected RNG, and grep shows no physics key in the GameConfig and no arcade import anywhere in src/. Introducing Arcade to get its 'optimizations' would move gameplay state into the scene layer and desync from the deterministic 24-seed harness.

items.title: The one real per-frame hotspot in THIS scene is stroke segment count, not entity count — thin drag points at the input boundary
items.claim: Official docs flag complex Graphics paths as the expensive case under WebGL (per-frame polygon decomposition). DuelScene.strokePinched issues a separate lineStyle+beginPath+moveTo+lineTo+strokePath per segment; a long drag stores up to 2048 world points (pointermove cap), and each live frame draws the stroke TWICE (body+core), plus every fading redStroke twice more and every trail twice — worst case tens of thousands of path commands in one frame during multi-stroke fades. This is the only load in the scene that scales unboundedly with player input. Pointer events arrive at display rate (up to 120+ Hz), far above any drawing fidelity the OG could show: the ledger's 15Hz content floor and the §S24-B reach cap both bound how much stroke detail the original ever rendered, so distance-based point decimation (drop points closer than ~2-3 world px) loses nothing measurable while collapsing worst-case segment count ~5-10x.

items.adjudication_reason: DuelScene pointermove already caps at dragPoints.length < 2048 but stores EVERY move event; strokePinched then draws per-segment for the live drag, redStrokes, and trails each frame — and COMBAT_MEASUREMENTS §00's '15 Hz content floor' plus §S24-B's rendered-stroke reach cap prove the OG never carried sub-pixel-dense stroke detail, so decimation cannot cost fidelity. Must be parameterized as a min-distance threshold in src/config/ (CONTRACT/INFERRED-tagged), not a magic number in the scene.
items.implementation_note: In the pointermove handler, skip the push when hypot(w - lastStored) < a new config/combat threshold (~2-3 world px, tag INFERRED, note the §S24-B reach cap as the bounding measurement). DrawnStroke and Sim.applyStroke consume the same array, so verify the 24-seed duel harness and gesture-classification tests stay green — decimation changes stroke.points fed to the Sim, which is why the threshold must be small and config-owned.

dead_ends: No Phaser 3.90-specific performance changelog entries found beyond the 3.70 roundPixels default flip (3.90 searches surfaced nothing render-perf-relevant). Found no forum/postmortem thread specifically quantifying Graphics strokePath per-segment cost — that item rests on the official 'complex shapes are expensive' guidance plus repo code reading. Did not fetch GitHub issue #6874 (roundPixels image scaling) — title from search results only. Arcade physics research was cut short deliberately: grep proved no physics engine exists in src/, making deeper sourcing pointless. The franzeus postmortem's headline finding (Canvas 30% faster than WebGL on a Pixel 5) could not be adopted: src/main.ts pins Phaser.WEBGL explicitly because the art direction needs WebGL-only Graphics gradients.
